 Camavinga fades at Real Madrid: seeks redemption against Leipzig 
 Go to the comments section Add to your bookmarks Share this article Eduardo Camavinga is going through a difficult spell at Real Madrid . Despite returning from international duty with France with renewed optimism after featuring in the opening matches of Zinedine Zidane’s new tenure, the midfielder has been unable to turn his situation around at the club and remains relegated to a supporting role.
 The midfielder was one of the new faces in Zidane’s first France squad. He featured in all four matches, played 204 minutes and started both victories over Belgium. However, the morale boost from his return to the national team has not translated into more opportunities at Real Madrid.
 OneFootball Videos
 Just 25 minutes since the international break
 Camavinga joined up with France after starting two of Real Madrid’s first seven matches. Since his return, the pattern has continued: he was on the bench for the next three games and played just 25 minutes.
 The midfielder played 13 minutes against Villarreal, did not feature against Roma and added another 12 minutes against Sevilla.
 According to the figures cited in the original report, Camavinga has played the fewest minutes of any first-team midfielder since the team returned to action after the international break. He trails Federico Valverde, Jude Bellingham, Arda Güler, Aurélien Tchouaméni and Bernardo Silva.
 He has only played more than Thiago Pitarch, who is registered with Castilla and has yet to make an appearance this season.
 A situation dating back to last season
 Camavinga’s struggles are not new. Injuries and doubts over his performances have disrupted his run in the team in recent months, leaving him as a backup option in the squad.
 In the closing stages of last season, the Frenchman started just five of Real Madrid’s 17 matches across LaLiga and the Champions League. His role diminished to the point that he fell behind Thiago Pitarch in the pecking order and was ultimately left out of France’s World Cup squad.
 Although José Mourinho has praised him, as he did after the victory over Málaga on August 30, those words have not translated into more playing time.
 Uncertainty over his future also surfaced during the summer transfer window, when his stay at Real Madrid was not guaranteed.
 Camavinga seeks a chance to turn things around
 During the latest France training camp, the player himself acknowledged the impact of missing out on the World Cup.
 “Missing the World Cup affected me. That kind of disappointment was new to me, but the most important thing is to pick yourself up,” the midfielder explained.
 Camavinga was also critical of his own performances: “I need to be more focused on the pitch and make fewer mistakes.”
 The Frenchman believes he still has time to turn things around and rediscover the form that made him an important part of the team. Now, the match against Leipzig offers another opportunity to show Mourinho that he can play a bigger role.
 For now, his return to the national team has not changed his circumstances at Real Madrid. Camavinga needs to make the most of the opportunities he gets to break out of a pattern that threatens to keep him on the fringes.
